``` {r setup, include=FALSE}
# ==============================================================================
# 1. Global Configuration & Environment
# ==============================================================================
# Note: knitr defaults buffer chunk output until completion. For long-running
# chunks (large LMM fits), we set R.options(progress = TRUE) and use
# flush.console() inside helpers (see flush_progress() below). When running
# interactively in RStudio (not via Knit), output is unbuffered automatically.
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE,
  warning = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,
  results = "markup"   # default; ensures plain text streams correctly
)
options(scipen = 999, digits = 4)
set.seed(2024)

# Version each run; original result directories remain reference inputs.
run_id <- getOption("ug.run_id", format(Sys.time(), "RandomStructure_%Y%m%d_%H%M%S"))
run_root <- here::here("results", run_id)
source(here::here("config", "random_structure_revision.R"), local = TRUE)

# Sum-to-zero contrasts: required for valid Type III ANOVA in the presence of
# interactions, and for interpretable zero-correlation random-effect parameterizations.
# Reference: Schad, Vasishth, Hohenstein, & Kliegl (2020) on contrast coding.
options(contrasts = c("contr.sum", "contr.poly"))

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Global Settings & Analysis Targets (SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Set experiment version to match upstream preprocessing pipeline output.
experiment_version <- getOption("ug.experiment", "E2")  # "E1" or "E2"

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Stage 2 covariate handling (revised 2026-06). Trait MODERATION (SVO + the six
# PID5BF+ domains) has been MOVED OUT of the EEG to the behavioral analysis
# (Sta_Behaviour_E1_E2_Integrative; per-experiment main-effect screen) -- a
# between-subjects trait x within-subjects design interaction is anticonservative
# and underpowered at n = 30 on single-trial ERPs. This sensitivity script keeps
# ONLY the rating nuisance-covariate control (Track C; Rating_1/2/3 as grand-
# mean-centered main effects).
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
rating_covariates <- c("Rating_1", "Rating_2", "Rating_3")

# Flat union for covariate loading (only ratings are needed now).
stage2_traits <- rating_covariates

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Trial-level inclusion criteria
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# These thresholds define which trials enter Stage 1 LMM analysis. They are
# applied AT THE ANALYSIS LAYER (in load_and_prep below), NOT in the upstream
# HU pipeline preprocessing. Rationale: the canonical trials.csv produced by
# HU pipeline reflects only EEG-artifact rejection (peak-to-peak > 200 uV
# marked as NaN); response-related and RT-range exclusions are analysis-
# specific decisions and are therefore implemented here for transparency.
#
# IMPORTANT: keep these constants synchronized with Sta_Behaviour_RefAlday.Rmd
# (rt_lower_ms / rt_upper_ms, lines 56-57) and with the primary Alday-framework
# analysis (Sta_EEG_OfferPhase_RefAlday.Rmd). Cross-modality and cross-method
# sample equivalence requires identical inclusion logic across all three
# scripts. These values also match the average_by query in upstream HU
# pipeline calls (Pipline_UG_OfferPhase.Rmd lines 181-236).
rt_lower_ms <- 300
rt_upper_ms <- 3000

# Post-hoc gating thresholds (v2: layered).
# Effects with omnibus interaction p < confirmatory_alpha enter the main report.
# Effects with confirmatory_alpha <= p < marginal_threshold are written to
# Supplementary as "marginal" simple-effect contrasts; they are NEVER reported
# as confirmatory evidence. p >= marginal_threshold: no simple-effect extraction.
confirmatory_alpha  <- 0.05
marginal_threshold  <- 0.10

# Component definitions per experimental design.
#
# The offer-locked analysis extracts two CONFIRMATORY components, present in
# BOTH experiments (E1 ∩ E2) and constituting the cross-experiment conceptual
# replication evidence:
#   FRN, P3.
#
# Status per component is propagated to REPRODUCIBILITY.txt and Methods
# paragraph. All components run the same Stage 1 LMM pipeline; the
# confirmatory/exploratory distinction is a reporting-layer label.
#
# CPP (response-locked) was previously included; v2 removes it as out of
# scope for the offer-phase analysis.
comp_csv <- here::here("config", "erp_components.csv")
if (!file.exists(comp_csv)) {
  stop(sprintf("Component config not found: %s", comp_csv))
}
comp_def <- readr::read_csv(comp_csv, show_col_types = FALSE)
comp_def <- comp_def[comp_def$experiment == experiment_version, ]
confirmatory_components <- comp_def$comp_name[comp_def$role == "confirmatory"]
exploratory_components  <- comp_def$comp_name[comp_def$role == "exploratory"]
analyze_stim_components <- getOption("ug.components", c(confirmatory_components, exploratory_components))

# Helper to return component status for downstream reporting.
component_status <- function(comp_name) {
  if (comp_name %in% confirmatory_components) "confirmatory"
  else if (comp_name %in% exploratory_components) {
    if (experiment_version == "E1") "exploratory_offer_locked"
    else "exploratory_E2_only"
  }
  else NA_character_
}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

if(!require("pacman")) install.packages("pacman")
pacman::p_load(
  here, readr, readxl, dplyr, tidyr, stringr, tibble, purrr,  # Data wrangling
  lme4, lmerTest,                                              # Modeling
  pbkrtest,                                                    # Kenward-Roger backend for lmerTest
  car, parameters, performance,                                # Diagnostics
  buildmer,                                                    # LRT-based structure search
  R.utils,                                                     # withTimeout for buildmer protection
  emmeans, effectsize,                                         # Marginal means, effect sizes
  sjPlot, sjmisc,                                              # tab_model, plot_model
  ggplot2, ggpubr, gridExtra,                                  # Publication visualization
  knitr, kableExtra,                                           # Markdown table rendering
  openxlsx                                                     # Legacy Excel export
)

# Inferential strategy: cascading method preference for LMM
# (Satterthwaite -> Kenward-Roger -> Wald). EEG analyses are pure LMM
# (Gaussian on amplitude in microvolts), so there is no GLMM branch.
# 
# Cascade rationale:
# (1) Satterthwaite F (lmerTest::anova): finite-DenDF F-test, preferred for
#     Type I error control at moderate N_subj (Luke 2017).
# (2) Kenward-Roger F (pbkrtest backend via lmerTest): conservative second-
#     order correction. Different numerical implementation than Satterthwaite,
#     can succeed when Satterthwaite hits Hessian inversion failure modes on
#     ZCP-form (e.g., (0 + factor | id)) random structures at large N.
# (3) Wald chi-square (car::Anova): final fallback. Anti-conservative for
#     finite N (Luke 2017 simulations show Type I error 6-8% at N_subj < 30
#     for omnibus tests). Logged in REPRODUCIBILITY.txt when invoked.
# 
# CRITICAL ENGINEERING DETAIL: lmerTest's Satterthwaite/KR dispatch requires
# the model object class to include "lmerModLmerTest". When fit via
# lme4::lmer() (rather than lmerTest::lmer()), the result is bare "lmerMod"
# and anova() falls through to lme4's base method which silently ignores
# the ddf argument and returns no Pr column. fit_stage1_bates therefore
# upgrades the final model class via lmerTest::as_lmerModLmerTest() before
# returning, and the ANOVA cascade independently re-checks. See bates-engine
# chunk for details.
# 
# Post-hoc contrasts via emmeans use asymptotic (z-test) df for computational
# stability on large datasets. At present DenDF magnitudes (DenDF >> 30),
# z-tests differ from Satterthwaite-based t-tests by less than 1% (Luke 2017).
emmeans::emm_options(lmerTest.limit = 1e7, pbkrtest.limit = 1e7,
                     lmer.df = "asymptotic")
options(lmerTest.limit = 1e7)
options(pbkrtest.limit = 1e7)

# Output directory tree organized by analytic stage and reporting target.
out_root            <- file.path(run_root, "EEG", paste0(experiment_version, "_TwoStage_Bates_Traditional"))
out_stage1          <- file.path(out_root, "Stage1_TrialLevel")
out_stage2          <- file.path(out_root, "Stage2_RatingControl")
out_stage2_covctrl  <- file.path(out_stage2, "Covariate_Control_Ratings")
out_tables          <- file.path(out_root, "Tables_Manuscript")
out_suppl           <- file.path(out_root, "Supplementary")
for (d in c(out_stage1, out_stage2, out_stage2_covctrl, out_tables, out_suppl)) {
  if (!dir.exists(d)) dir.create(d, recursive = TRUE)
}

cat(sprintf("Pipeline initialized for Experiment: %s\nRoot: %s\n", experiment_version, out_root))
cat(sprintf("Stage 2 (EEG sensitivity): rating nuisance-covariate control only.\n"))
cat(sprintf("  Nuisance covariates / control model (%d): %s\n",
            length(rating_covariates), paste(rating_covariates, collapse = ", ")))

# Visual theme.
theme_set(theme_bw(base_size = 14) +
          theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), legend.position = "top"))

colors_emo <- c('neu'="#8491B4",'aff'="#91D1C2",'dis'="#E64B35",'dom'="#F39B7F",'enj'="#3C5488")
labels_emo <- c('neu'='Neutral','aff'='Affiliative','dis'='Disgust','dom'='Dominance','enj'='Reward')
colors_off <- c('fair'="#2E86AB",'unfair'="#A23B72")
labels_off <- c('fair'='Fair', 'unfair'='Unfair')

custom_control <- lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", optCtrl = list(maxfun = 200000), calc.derivs = FALSE)
custom_control_final <- lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", optCtrl = list(maxfun = 200000), calc.derivs = TRUE)

# Null-coalescing helper for safe attribute fallback.
`%||%` <- function(a, b) if (is.null(a)) b else a

capture_canonical_input <- function(path, label, expected_suffix) {
  if (!file.exists(path)) stop(sprintf("Input file not found for %s: %s", label, path))
  resolved <- normalizePath(path, winslash = "/", mustWork = TRUE)
  resolved_lower <- tolower(resolved)
  forbidden <- c("/previousresults/", "/olderbehaviourresults/", "/older/")
  if (any(vapply(forbidden, grepl, logical(1), x = resolved_lower, fixed = TRUE))) {
    stop(sprintf("Forbidden stale input path for %s: %s", label, resolved))
  }
  expected_suffix <- tolower(gsub("\\\\", "/", expected_suffix))
  if (!endsWith(resolved_lower, expected_suffix)) {
    stop(sprintf(
      "Non-canonical input for %s.\nExpected suffix: %s\nResolved path: %s",
      label, expected_suffix, resolved
    ))
  }
  info <- file.info(resolved)
  provenance <- list(
    label = label,
    path = resolved,
    modified = format(info$mtime, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S %Z"),
    bytes = as.numeric(info$size),
    md5 = unname(tools::md5sum(resolved))
  )
  cat(sprintf(
    "[Input %s] %s | modified=%s | bytes=%s | md5=%s\n",
    label, provenance$path, provenance$modified,
    format(provenance$bytes, scientific = FALSE), provenance$md5
  ))
  provenance
}

write_input_provenance <- function(provenance) {
  if (is.null(provenance)) stop("Canonical input provenance was not captured.")
  cat("## Canonical preprocessing input:\n")
  cat("Label:   ", provenance$label, "\n")
  cat("Path:    ", provenance$path, "\n")
  cat("Modified:", provenance$modified, "\n")
  cat("Bytes:   ", format(provenance$bytes, scientific = FALSE), "\n")
  cat("MD5:     ", provenance$md5, "\n\n")
}

add_random_contrast_columns <- function(data, random_vars, group_name) {
  # Include the full factorial of the specified within-participant variables.
  # Numeric sum-contrast columns make both main and interaction ZCP blocks diagonal.
  stopifnot(length(random_vars) > 0L, !anyDuplicated(random_vars))
  if (!all(c(random_vars, group_name) %in% names(data))) {
    stop("Missing random-design or grouping variable.")
  }
  design_data <- data[random_vars]
  contrast_args <- list()
  for (v in random_vars) {
    x <- design_data[[v]]
    if (anyNA(x)) stop("Missing values in random-design variable: ", v)
    if (is.factor(x)) {
      if (nlevels(x) < 2L) stop("Random-design factor has fewer than two levels: ", v)
      contrast_args[[v]] <- contr.sum(nlevels(x))
    } else if (is.numeric(x)) {
      if (any(!is.finite(x))) stop("Non-finite random-design variable: ", v)
      design_data[[v]] <- x - mean(x)
    } else stop("Unsupported random-slope variable type: ", v)
  }
  design_formula <- reformulate(paste(random_vars, collapse = " * "))
  mm <- model.matrix(design_formula, data = design_data,
                     contrasts.arg = if (length(contrast_args)) contrast_args else NULL)
  assignments <- attr(mm, "assign")
  labels <- attr(terms(design_formula), "term.labels")
  random_terms <- random_columns <- random_blocks <- character(0)
  for (k in seq_along(labels)) {
    indices <- which(assignments == k)
    term_name <- gsub(":", "_x_", labels[k], fixed = TRUE)
    for (j in seq_along(indices)) {
      column_name <- sprintf("RE_%s_%d", term_name, j)
      data[[column_name]] <- mm[, indices[j]]
      random_columns <- c(random_columns, column_name)
      random_blocks[column_name] <- paste0(term_name, "_slope_block")
      random_terms <- c(random_terms, sprintf("(0 + %s | %s)", column_name, group_name))
    }
  }
  list(data = data, random_terms = random_terms,
       random_columns = random_columns, random_blocks = random_blocks)
}

make_blocked_buildmer_terms <- function(formula, random_blocks) {
  terms <- buildmer::tabulate.formula(formula)
  for (column_name in names(random_blocks)) {
    is_random_column <- !is.na(terms$grouping) & terms$term == column_name
    terms$block[is_random_column] <- unname(random_blocks[[column_name]])
  }
  terms
}

final_lmm_diagnostics <- function(model) {
  optimizer_code <- model@optinfo$conv$opt %||% NA_integer_
  convergence_messages <- model@optinfo$conv$lme4$messages %||% character(0)
  hessian <- model@optinfo$derivs$Hessian
  hessian_available <- !is.null(hessian)
  hessian_positive_definite <- if (hessian_available) {
    eigenvalues <- tryCatch(
      eigen(hessian, symmetric = TRUE, only.values = TRUE)$values,
      error = function(e) NA_real_
    )
    all(is.finite(eigenvalues)) && min(eigenvalues) > 0
  } else FALSE
  fixed_se <- sqrt(diag(vcov(model)))
  diagnostics <- list(
    optimizer_code = optimizer_code,
    convergence_messages = paste(convergence_messages, collapse = " | "),
    singular = lme4::isSingular(model, tol = 1e-4),
    hessian_available = hessian_available,
    hessian_positive_definite = hessian_positive_definite,
    finite_fixed_se = length(fixed_se) > 0 && all(is.finite(fixed_se)),
    finite_likelihood = is.finite(AIC(model)) && is.finite(as.numeric(logLik(model)))
  )
  hard_message_pattern <- paste(
    c("failed to converge", "unable to evaluate scaled gradient",
      "degenerate.*Hessian", "negative eigenvalue"),
    collapse = "|"
  )
  messages_ok <- !any(grepl(
    hard_message_pattern, convergence_messages, ignore.case = TRUE
  ))
  diagnostics$valid <- isTRUE(diagnostics$optimizer_code == 0) &&
    messages_ok &&
    !diagnostics$singular && diagnostics$hessian_available &&
    diagnostics$hessian_positive_definite && diagnostics$finite_fixed_se &&
    diagnostics$finite_likelihood
  diagnostics
}

format_final_lmm_diagnostics <- function(d) {
  sprintf(
    paste0("valid=%s; optimizer_code=%s; messages=%s; singular=%s; ",
           "hessian_available=%s; hessian_positive_definite=%s; ",
           "finite_fixed_se=%s; finite_likelihood=%s"),
    d$valid, d$optimizer_code,
    ifelse(nchar(d$convergence_messages) == 0, "none", d$convergence_messages),
    d$singular, d$hessian_available, d$hessian_positive_definite,
    d$finite_fixed_se, d$finite_likelihood
  )
}

refit_and_validate_final_lmm <- function(model, data) {
  attrs_to_keep <- attributes(model)[c("step4_selected", "step4_lrt_table")]
  fit_and_check <- function(candidate_formula, random_tier) {
    candidate <- lme4::lmer(
      candidate_formula, data = data, REML = TRUE,
      control = custom_control_final
    )
    for (an in names(attrs_to_keep)) {
      if (!is.null(attrs_to_keep[[an]])) attr(candidate, an) <- attrs_to_keep[[an]]
    }
    attr(candidate, "final_validation") <- final_lmm_diagnostics(candidate)
    attr(candidate, "final_random_tier") <- random_tier
    candidate
  }

  exact <- fit_and_check(formula(model), "selected_formula")
  if (isTRUE(attr(exact, "final_validation")$valid)) return(exact)

  stop("The exact buildmer-selected LMM failed the acceptance gate: ",
       format_final_lmm_diagnostics(attr(exact, "final_validation")))
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Buildmer engineering helpers (defensive against deadlock on large datasets).
# 
# When N > 20K trials, lmerTest can cause buildmer's iterative LRT loop to hang
# (CPU 0%) because every internal anova() call triggers Satterthwaite Hessian
# inversion. We detach lmerTest before buildmer and reattach after. We also
# wrap buildmer in withTimeout to prevent unbounded waits.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
detach_lmerTest_safely <- function() {
  if ("package:lmerTest" %in% search()) {
    detach("package:lmerTest", unload = FALSE, character.only = FALSE)
    return(TRUE)
  }
  FALSE
}

reattach_lmerTest_safely <- function(was_detached) {
  if (isTRUE(was_detached)) suppressMessages(library(lmerTest))
  invisible(NULL)
}

run_buildmer_protected <- function(buildmer_fn, ..., timeout_sec = 1800) {
  was_lmerTest <- detach_lmerTest_safely()
  on.exit(reattach_lmerTest_safely(was_lmerTest), add = TRUE)
  
  result <- tryCatch({
    R.utils::withTimeout({
      buildmer_fn(...)
    }, timeout = timeout_sec, onTimeout = "error")
  }, TimeoutException = function(ex) {
    msg <- sprintf("buildmer exceeded %d seconds", timeout_sec)
    progress_log(sprintf("[TIMEOUT] %s; aborting.", msg), indent = 2)
    structure(
      list(type = "timeout", message = msg),
      class = "buildmer_failure"
    )
  }, error = function(e) {
    msg <- conditionMessage(e)
    if (grepl("reached.*time.*limit|timeout", msg, ignore.case = TRUE)) {
      progress_log(sprintf("[TIMEOUT] buildmer exceeded %d seconds; aborting.",
                           timeout_sec), indent = 2)
      structure(
        list(type = "timeout", message = msg),
        class = "buildmer_failure"
      )
    } else {
      progress_log(sprintf("[WARN] buildmer error: %s", msg),
                   indent = 2)
      structure(
        list(type = "error", message = msg),
        class = "buildmer_failure"
      )
    }
  })
  
  result
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Progress reporting helpers.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# R Markdown can buffer cat() output until a chunk finishes, hiding progress
# during long-running operations. flush_progress() forces immediate display.
# Wall-clock timing is captured per stage to give the user realistic runtime
# expectations on subsequent components.
flush_progress <- function() {
  flush.console()
  if (interactive()) Sys.sleep(0)  # nominal yield
}

progress_log <- function(msg, indent = 0) {
  prefix <- strrep("  ", indent)
  cat(sprintf("%s%s\n", prefix, msg))
  flush_progress()
}

# Format an elapsed-time delta for log lines. Used to report duration of
# expensive operations (model fits, ANOVA, buildmer search).
format_elapsed <- function(t_start) {
  secs <- as.numeric(Sys.time() - t_start, units = "secs")
  if (secs < 60) sprintf("%.1fs", secs)
  else if (secs < 3600) sprintf("%dm%02ds", floor(secs / 60), round(secs %% 60))
  else sprintf("%dh%02dm", floor(secs / 3600), floor((secs %% 3600) / 60))
}

# Wrap an expression with start/end progress logs and elapsed time.
with_progress <- function(label, expr, indent = 1) {
  progress_log(sprintf("[%s] starting...", label), indent = indent)
  t0 <- Sys.time()
  result <- force(expr)
  progress_log(sprintf("[%s] done (%s).", label, format_elapsed(t0)),
               indent = indent)
  result
}
```

``` {r apa-module}
# ==============================================================================
# 2. Helper Functions (preserved from original script).
# ==============================================================================

# APA display formatter for p values in manuscript-facing tables.
format_p_apa <- function(p, include_equals = FALSE) {
  out <- rep("-", length(p))
  valid <- !is.na(p)
  out[valid & p < .001] <- "< .001"
  exact <- valid & p >= .001
  out[exact] <- sub("^0", "", sprintf("%.3f", p[exact]))
  if (include_equals) out[exact] <- paste("=", out[exact])
  out
}

is_p_value_column <- function(column_name) {
  grepl("^p($|[._-])", column_name, ignore.case = TRUE) ||
    grepl("^Pr\\(>", column_name, ignore.case = TRUE)
}

# Universal type conversion, missing-value handling, and column purging.
kill_scipen <- function(df) {
  df %>%
    dplyr::mutate(across(where(is.factor), as.character)) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(across(everything(), function(vec) {
      if (is.numeric(vec) && is_p_value_column(dplyr::cur_column())) {
        vec <- format_p_apa(vec)
      } else if (is.numeric(vec)) {
        vec <- format(round(vec, 4), scientific = FALSE, trim = TRUE)
      }
      vec <- ifelse(is.infinite(suppressWarnings(as.numeric(vec))), "Inf", vec)
      vec <- ifelse(is.na(vec) | vec == "NA", "-", as.character(vec))
      vec
    })) %>%
    dplyr::select(where(~ !all(. == "-")))
}

# APA significance star generator.
add_sig_stars <- function(p) {
  dplyr::case_when(
    is.na(p)  ~ "-",
    p < 0.001 ~ "***",
    p < 0.01  ~ "**",
    p < 0.05  ~ "*",
    p < 0.1   ~ ".",
    TRUE      ~ "ns"
  )
}

# Map sum-coding suffixes back to interpretable factor-level labels.
beautify_labels <- function(df) {
  dict <- c(
    "\\bemotion1\\b"    = "emotion[neu-grand]",
    "\\bemotion2\\b"    = "emotion[aff-grand]",
    "\\bemotion3\\b"    = "emotion[dis-grand]",
    "\\bemotion4\\b"    = "emotion[dom-grand]",
    "\\boffer_type1\\b" = "offer_type[fair-grand]"
  )
  df %>% dplyr::mutate(across(where(is.character),
                              ~ stringr::str_replace_all(., dict)))
}

# Format ANOVA table to APA strings.
# v2: appends partial eta-squared with 95% CI for LMM (Gaussian) models.
# Effect-size computation uses effectsize::eta_squared() which handles
# both lme4 and lmerTest model classes. EEG analyses are pure LMM, so
# eta-squared is always meaningful here (no GLMM branch).
format_anova_apa <- function(anova_obj, model = NULL) {
  df_res <- as.data.frame(anova_obj) %>%
    tibble::rownames_to_column("Effect")
  
  get_col <- function(col_name) {
    if (col_name %in% names(df_res)) df_res[[col_name]] else rep(NA, nrow(df_res))
  }
  
  df_res <- df_res %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      F_val  = get_col("F value"),
      NumDF  = get_col("NumDF"),
      DenDF  = get_col("DenDF"),
      Df_val = get_col("Df"),
      Chisq  = get_col("Chisq"),
      p_val  = dplyr::case_when(
        !is.na(get_col("Pr(>F)"))     ~ get_col("Pr(>F)"),
        !is.na(get_col("Pr(>Chisq)")) ~ get_col("Pr(>Chisq)"),
        TRUE ~ NA_real_
      ),
      Sig = add_sig_stars(p_val),
      p_str = format_p_apa(p_val, include_equals = TRUE),
      APA_Report = dplyr::case_when(
        !is.na(F_val) & !is.na(NumDF) & !is.na(DenDF) ~
          sprintf("F(%s, %.2f) = %.2f, p %s", NumDF, DenDF, F_val, p_str),
        !is.na(F_val) & !is.na(NumDF) ~
          sprintf("F(%s) = %.2f, p %s", NumDF, F_val, p_str),
        !is.na(Chisq) & !is.na(Df_val) ~
          sprintf("\u03C7\u00B2(%s) = %.2f, p %s", Df_val, Chisq, p_str),
        TRUE ~ "[stat unrecognized]"
      )
    )
  
  # Partial eta-squared with 95% CI. Only computed for F-statistic rows
  # (LMM Satterthwaite/KR). Wald chi-square fallback rows show "-".
  eta_str <- rep("-", nrow(df_res))
  if (!is.null(model) && inherits(model, "merMod")) {
    eta_tab <- tryCatch(
      effectsize::eta_squared(anova_obj, partial = TRUE, ci = 0.95,
                              alternative = "two.sided"),
      error = function(e) NULL
    )
    if (!is.null(eta_tab) && nrow(eta_tab) > 0) {
      eta_df <- as.data.frame(eta_tab)
      param_col <- intersect(c("Parameter", "Effect"), names(eta_df))[1]
      eta_col   <- intersect(c("Eta2_partial", "Eta2"), names(eta_df))[1]
      lo_col    <- "CI_low"
      hi_col    <- "CI_high"
      if (!is.na(param_col) && !is.na(eta_col) &&
          all(c(lo_col, hi_col) %in% names(eta_df))) {
        for (i in seq_len(nrow(df_res))) {
          eff_name <- df_res$Effect[i]
          match_idx <- which(eta_df[[param_col]] == eff_name)
          if (length(match_idx) == 1) {
            eta_str[i] <- sprintf("%.3f [%.3f, %.3f]",
                                  eta_df[[eta_col]][match_idx],
                                  eta_df[[lo_col]][match_idx],
                                  eta_df[[hi_col]][match_idx])
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
  df_res$eta2_partial_95CI <- eta_str
  
  df_res <- df_res %>%
    dplyr::select(Effect, APA_Report, eta2_partial_95CI, Sig, p_val)
  kill_scipen(beautify_labels(df_res))
}

# Format post-hoc emmeans output to APA strings.
# v2: appends 95% CI columns. EEG analyses operate on raw amplitude scale
# (microvolts, Gaussian), so no scale transformation (no OR, no percent
# change) is needed -- contrasts are reported directly in microvolts.
# Switches to z-statistic notation when df is infinite (asymptotic case).
format_posthoc_apa <- function(emm_df) {
  df_clean <- as.data.frame(emm_df)
  
  est_col <- intersect(names(df_clean),
                       c("estimate", "emmean", "response"))
  if (length(est_col) == 0) {
    trend_col <- grep("\\.trend$", names(df_clean), value = TRUE)
    est_col <- if (length(trend_col) > 0) trend_col[1] else names(df_clean)[2]
  } else {
    est_col <- est_col[1]
  }
  
  # CI columns. emmeans summary(infer=c(TRUE,TRUE)) emits CL columns, but
  # column naming varies:
  #   - "lower.CL" / "upper.CL"      (most cases)
  #   - "asymp.LCL" / "asymp.UCL"    (when df is Inf, e.g. asymptotic mode)
  # If neither is present (rare; happens when summary infer didn't fire),
  # synthesize from estimate +/- 1.96*SE (Wald-based asymptotic CI). This
  # ensures lower.CL / upper.CL columns ALWAYS exist, which matters because
  # dplyr::case_when() evaluates ALL RHS expressions regardless of LHS truth
  # value -- a missing column would error even on rows where the expression
  # is "not selected".
  if (all(c("lower.CL", "upper.CL") %in% names(df_clean))) {
    # already correctly named
  } else if (all(c("asymp.LCL", "asymp.UCL") %in% names(df_clean))) {
    df_clean$lower.CL <- df_clean$asymp.LCL
    df_clean$upper.CL <- df_clean$asymp.UCL
  } else if ("SE" %in% names(df_clean)) {
    # Synthesize Wald CI. Mark as fallback in case downstream wants to flag.
    df_clean$lower.CL <- df_clean[[est_col]] - 1.96 * df_clean$SE
    df_clean$upper.CL <- df_clean[[est_col]] + 1.96 * df_clean$SE
  } else {
    # No SE either: emit NA columns to keep the schema stable.
    df_clean$lower.CL <- NA_real_
    df_clean$upper.CL <- NA_real_
  }
  has_ci <- all(c("lower.CL", "upper.CL") %in% names(df_clean)) &&
            !all(is.na(df_clean$lower.CL))
  
  df_clean <- df_clean %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      Sig = add_sig_stars(p.value),
      p_str = format_p_apa(p.value, include_equals = TRUE)
    )
  
  # Stats_String: with CI when available, fall back to no-CI form otherwise.
  # Unit hint "muV" because EEG amplitudes are in microvolts.
  if ("t.ratio" %in% names(df_clean)) {
    df_clean <- df_clean %>% dplyr::mutate(
      Stats_String = dplyr::case_when(
        has_ci & is.infinite(df) ~ sprintf(
          "b = %.2f muV (SE = %.2f), 95%% CI [%.3f, %.3f], z = %.2f, p %s",
          .data[[est_col]], SE, lower.CL, upper.CL, t.ratio, p_str),
        has_ci ~ sprintf(
          "b = %.2f muV (SE = %.2f), 95%% CI [%.3f, %.3f], t(%.2f) = %.2f, p %s",
          .data[[est_col]], SE, lower.CL, upper.CL, df, t.ratio, p_str),
        is.infinite(df) ~ sprintf(
          "b = %.2f muV (SE = %.2f), z = %.2f, p %s",
          .data[[est_col]], SE, t.ratio, p_str),
        TRUE ~ sprintf(
          "b = %.2f muV (SE = %.2f), t(%.2f) = %.2f, p %s",
          .data[[est_col]], SE, df, t.ratio, p_str)
      )
    )
  } else if ("z.ratio" %in% names(df_clean)) {
    df_clean <- df_clean %>% dplyr::mutate(
      Stats_String = dplyr::case_when(
        has_ci ~ sprintf(
          "b = %.2f muV (SE = %.2f), 95%% CI [%.3f, %.3f], z = %.2f, p %s",
          .data[[est_col]], SE, lower.CL, upper.CL, z.ratio, p_str),
        TRUE ~ sprintf(
          "b = %.2f muV (SE = %.2f), z = %.2f, p %s",
          .data[[est_col]], SE, z.ratio, p_str)
      )
    )
  } else {
    df_clean <- df_clean %>% dplyr::mutate(
      Stats_String = dplyr::case_when(
        has_ci ~ sprintf(
          "b = %.2f muV (SE = %.2f), 95%% CI [%.3f, %.3f], p %s",
          .data[[est_col]], SE, lower.CL, upper.CL, p_str),
        TRUE ~ sprintf(
          "b = %.2f muV (SE = %.2f), p %s",
          .data[[est_col]], SE, p_str)
      )
    )
  }
  
  if (has_ci) {
    df_clean <- df_clean %>%
      dplyr::mutate(CI_str = sprintf("[%.3f, %.3f]", lower.CL, upper.CL))
  }
  
  df_clean <- df_clean %>%
    dplyr::select(-p_str) %>%
    dplyr::relocate(Sig, .after = Stats_String)
  kill_scipen(beautify_labels(df_clean))
}

# Extract fixed-effect coefficients with safe fallback.
format_coefs <- function(model) {
  tryCatch({
    coefs <- as.data.frame(parameters::parameters(model, effects = "fixed"))
    coefs %>% beautify_labels() %>% kill_scipen()
  }, error = function(e) {
    as.data.frame(summary(model)$coefficients) %>%
      tibble::rownames_to_column("Predictor") %>%
      beautify_labels() %>% kill_scipen()
  })
}
```

``` {r prep-functions}
# ==============================================================================
# 3. Data Loading & Cleaning
# ==============================================================================

standardize_id <- function(ids) {
  sprintf("Vp%04d", as.numeric(stringr::str_extract(ids, "\\d+")))
}

# Covariate loader. Retains raw (un-Z-scored) trait values; Stage 2 standardization
# happens inside the Stage 2 function where scoping is unambiguous.
load_covariates <- function(path_cov) {
  if (is.na(path_cov) || !file.exists(path_cov)) {
    warning("Covariate file unavailable; Stage 2 will be skipped.")
    return(NULL)
  }
  cat(sprintf("[Covariates] Loading: %s\n", basename(path_cov)))
  
  df_cov <- if (grepl("\\.csv$", path_cov)) {
    readr::read_csv(path_cov, show_col_types = FALSE)
  } else {
    readxl::read_excel(path_cov)
  }
  
  names(df_cov)[1] <- "raw_id"
  df_cov$participant_id <- standardize_id(df_cov$raw_id)
  
  df_cov_clean <- df_cov %>%
    dplyr::select(participant_id, dplyr::any_of(c("SVO_type", stage2_traits)))
  
  cat(sprintf("[Covariates] N = %d subjects, %d traits available.\n",
              nrow(df_cov_clean),
              sum(stage2_traits %in% names(df_cov_clean))))
  df_cov_clean
}

# ERP component loader and cleaner.
#
# Baseline preprocessing: mean-centered (NOT z-scored). Per Alday (2019), keeping
# baseline in microvolt units allows direct comparison with the published
# coefficient plots (Fig. 10) and preserves interpretation of beta_baseline as
# 'fraction of pre-stimulus drift propagated forward'.
#
# Outlier filter |amplitude| < 200 microvolts: in the Alday baseline-as-covariate
# framework, extreme target-window values often arise from baseline drift that
# the model can absorb. This filter is therefore conservative; the number of
# trimmed trials is logged for the manuscript Methods section.
load_and_prep <- function(path_erp, df_covariates, erp_name, baseline_col) {
  if (!file.exists(path_erp)) {
    stop(sprintf("ERP file missing: %s", path_erp))
  }
  
  df <- readr::read_csv(path_erp, show_col_types = FALSE)
  
  # reaction and RT are required for the trial-level inclusion criteria
  # applied below; participant_id, Offers_Other, emotion, and index are
  # required for condition coding and downstream key construction.
  required_cols <- c("participant_id", "Offers_Other", "emotion", "index",
                     "reaction", "RT")
  missing_cols <- setdiff(required_cols, names(df))
  if (length(missing_cols) > 0) {
    stop(sprintf("Required columns missing from %s: %s",
                 basename(path_erp), paste(missing_cols, collapse = ", ")))
  }
  
  if (!(erp_name %in% names(df))) {
    cat(sprintf("[SKIP] Component '%s' absent from data.\n", erp_name))
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  df$participant_id <- standardize_id(df$participant_id)
  
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Apply trial inclusion criteria with logging.
  # 
  # Three sequential filters mirror those in Sta_Behaviour_RefAlday.Rmd
  # (load_and_prep_behavior, lines 605-622) to ensure cross-modality sample
  # equivalence; they also match the primary Alday-framework analysis
  # (Sta_EEG_OfferPhase_RefAlday.Rmd) for cross-method sample equivalence.
  #   (1) standard fair/unfair offer pairs (excludes 7:3 medium-fairness filler);
  #   (2) reaction != 0 (excludes timeout / no-response trials);
  #   (3) RT within [rt_lower_ms, rt_upper_ms] (excludes premature responses
  #       and response-window-exceeding trials).
  # 
  # These filters are applied at the analysis layer rather than in upstream
  # HU pipeline preprocessing, for the reason given in the inclusion-criteria
  # block at the top of the setup chunk.
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  n_orig <- nrow(df)
  
  # Filter 1: standard fair/unfair offers only.
  df <- df %>% dplyr::filter(Offers_Other %in% c(5, 6, 8, 9))
  cat(sprintf("[Filter] %s | Offers_Other in {5,6,8,9}: %d -> %d trials (%d removed)\n",
              erp_name, n_orig, nrow(df), n_orig - nrow(df)))
  
  # Filter 2: exclude reaction == 0 (timeout / missing response).
  n_pre <- nrow(df)
  df <- df %>% dplyr::filter(reaction != 0)
  cat(sprintf("[Filter] %s | reaction != 0 (timeout): %d -> %d trials (%d removed)\n",
              erp_name, n_pre, nrow(df), n_pre - nrow(df)))
  
  # Filter 3: RT range.
  n_pre <- nrow(df)
  df <- df %>% dplyr::filter(RT >= rt_lower_ms, RT <= rt_upper_ms)
  cat(sprintf("[Filter] %s | RT in [%d, %d] ms: %d -> %d trials (%d removed)\n",
              erp_name, rt_lower_ms, rt_upper_ms,
              n_pre, nrow(df), n_pre - nrow(df)))
  
  df <- df %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      offer_type = factor(
        dplyr::case_when(
          Offers_Other %in% c(5, 6) ~ "fair",
          Offers_Other %in% c(8, 9) ~ "unfair"
        ),
        levels = c("fair", "unfair")
      ),
      emotion = factor(emotion, levels = c("neu", "aff", "dis", "dom", "enj"))
    )
  
  orig_n <- nrow(df)
  df <- df %>% dplyr::filter(abs(.data[[erp_name]]) < 200)
  if (orig_n > nrow(df)) {
    cat(sprintf("[QC] %s: removed %d trials with |amplitude| > 200 \u00B5V (%.1f%%).\n",
                erp_name, orig_n - nrow(df), 100 * (orig_n - nrow(df)) / orig_n))
  }
  
  # Traditional baseline subtraction: amplitude has already been baseline-
  # corrected upstream in preprocessing (epoch minus mean of -200 to 0 ms).
  # No Baseline_c column is needed in the model; we explicitly omit any
  # baseline handling here. baseline_col argument is accepted for API
  # compatibility with the Alday version of this loader but ignored.
  if (!is.null(baseline_col)) {
    cat(sprintf("[Note] %s: ignoring baseline_col '%s'; data is already baseline-corrected upstream.\n",
                basename(path_erp), baseline_col))
  }
  
  if (!is.null(df_covariates)) {
    df <- dplyr::left_join(df, df_covariates, by = "participant_id")
  }
  
  df
}

check_uniqueness <- function(df, context_name) {
  if (nrow(df) != dplyr::n_distinct(dplyr::select(df, participant_id, index))) {
    stop(sprintf("CRITICAL: duplicate (participant_id, index) keys in %s.", context_name))
  }
}

# LMM residual-assumption diagnostics (Meteyard & Davies 2020, Table 7
# "Assumptions": report whether the fitted LMM meets assumptions). At single-
# trial N, formal normality tests (e.g. Shapiro-Wilk) are over-powered, so
# residual normality is assessed descriptively (skewness and excess kurtosis ~ 0
# under normality) and graphically (a best-effort Q-Q + residual-vs-fitted PDF).
# Homoscedasticity is indexed by the Spearman correlation between |residual| and
# fitted value. Writes assumptions_<label>.md (+ .pdf) into out_dir.
lmm_assumption_diagnostics <- function(model, label, out_dir) {
  r <- tryCatch(stats::residuals(model), error = function(e) NULL)
  f <- tryCatch(stats::fitted(model),    error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(r) || is.null(f) || length(r) < 3) return(invisible(NULL))
  if (!dir.exists(out_dir)) dir.create(out_dir, recursive = TRUE)
  mu <- mean(r); v <- mean((r - mu)^2)
  skew   <- if (v > 0) mean((r - mu)^3) / v^1.5 else NA_real_
  exkurt <- if (v > 0) mean((r - mu)^4) / v^2 - 3 else NA_real_
  homo_rho <- suppressWarnings(tryCatch(
    stats::cor(abs(r), f, method = "spearman"), error = function(e) NA_real_))
  tbl <- data.frame(
    Label = label, N_residuals = length(r),
    Residual_skewness = round(skew, 3),
    Residual_excess_kurtosis = round(exkurt, 3),
    Homoscedasticity_rho_absResid_fitted = round(homo_rho, 3),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  tryCatch({
    grDevices::pdf(file.path(out_dir, sprintf("assumptions_%s.pdf", label)),
                   width = 9, height = 4.5)
    op <- graphics::par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
    stats::qqnorm(r, pch = ".", main = sprintf("%s: residual Q-Q", label))
    stats::qqline(r, col = "red")
    plot(f, r, pch = ".", xlab = "Fitted", ylab = "Residual",
         main = "Residual vs fitted"); graphics::abline(h = 0, col = "red")
    graphics::par(op); grDevices::dev.off()
  }, error = function(e) try(grDevices::dev.off(), silent = TRUE))
  writeLines(c(
    sprintf("# LMM residual-assumption diagnostics: %s", label),
    sprintf("Generated: %s", format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")),
    "",
    "Whether the fitted LMM meets residual assumptions (Meteyard & Davies, 2020,",
    "Table 7). At single-trial N, formal normality tests (e.g. Shapiro-Wilk) are",
    "over-powered, so normality is assessed descriptively (skewness and excess",
    "kurtosis are ~0 under normality) and graphically (assumptions_*.pdf: Q-Q and",
    "residual-vs-fitted). The homoscedasticity index is the Spearman correlation",
    "between |residual| and fitted value (near 0 = homoscedastic).",
    "",
    knitr::kable(tbl, format = "markdown", row.names = FALSE)
  ), file.path(out_dir, sprintf("assumptions_%s.md", label)))
  invisible(tbl)
}

# Baseline pre-check: tests whether mean baseline differs across emotion x
# offer_type cells. Pure diagnostic. Does NOT gate the main analysis -- the
# Alday framework explicitly allows baseline-condition interactions and the
# main pipeline tests those interactions via LRT in fit_stage1_bates. This
# helper exists to:
#   (a) flag potential confounds for transparency in the Methods paragraph;
#   (b) provide a single number (omnibus interaction F) to cite when
#       reviewers ask "was baseline balanced across conditions?".
# Output written to Supplementary/baseline_balance/<component>.md.
# 
# Implementation note: uses the same LMM machinery as the main analysis
# (lmer + Type III F via Satterthwaite cascade) for methodological
# consistency. Each call adds ~10-30 seconds to runtime; total overhead
# across all components is < 3 minutes, negligible vs the Bates pipeline
# itself.
pre_check_baseline_balance <- function(data, comp_name, out_dir) {
  if (!"Baseline_c" %in% names(data)) {
    cat(sprintf("[PreCheck] %s: Baseline_c absent; skipping balance check.\n",
                comp_name))
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  
  if (!dir.exists(out_dir)) dir.create(out_dir, recursive = TRUE)
  out_path <- file.path(out_dir, sprintf("%s_baseline_balance.md", comp_name))
  
  cat(sprintf("[PreCheck] %s: testing baseline ~ emotion * offer_type ...\n",
              comp_name))
  
  fit <- tryCatch({
    bf <- lmerTest::lmer(
      Baseline_c ~ emotion * offer_type + (1 | participant_id),
      data = data, REML = TRUE
    )
    bf
  }, error = function(e) {
    cat(sprintf("[PreCheck] %s: model failed (%s).\n",
                comp_name, conditionMessage(e)))
    NULL
  })
  if (is.null(fit)) return(invisible(NULL))
  
  # Class upgrade defensive (lmerTest::lmer should already produce
  # lmerModLmerTest, but check for safety).
  if (!inherits(fit, "lmerModLmerTest")) {
    fit <- tryCatch(lmerTest::as_lmerModLmerTest(fit), error = function(e) fit)
  }
  
  res <- tryCatch(
    suppressWarnings(anova(fit, type = 3, ddf = "Satterthwaite")),
    error = function(e) NULL
  )
  if (is.null(res) || !any(grepl("^Pr", colnames(res)))) {
    res <- tryCatch(
      suppressWarnings(anova(fit, type = 3, ddf = "Kenward-Roger")),
      error = function(e) NULL
    )
  }
  if (is.null(res)) {
    res <- tryCatch(car::Anova(fit, type = 3, test.statistic = "F"),
                    error = function(e) NULL)
  }
  
  apa_tab <- if (!is.null(res)) format_anova_apa(res, model = fit) else NULL
  
  # Extract the omnibus emotion:offer_type p-value if present, for a
  # one-line summary.
  interaction_p <- if (!is.null(apa_tab)) {
    int_row <- apa_tab[apa_tab$Effect == "emotion:offer_type", , drop = FALSE]
    if (nrow(int_row) == 1) int_row$p_val else NA_real_
  } else NA_real_
  
  cell_means <- data %>%
    dplyr::group_by(emotion, offer_type) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(
      mean_baseline = mean(Baseline_c, na.rm = TRUE),
      sd_baseline   = sd(Baseline_c, na.rm = TRUE),
      n_trials      = dplyr::n(),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
  
  writeLines(c(
    sprintf("# Baseline Balance Pre-Check: %s", comp_name),
    sprintf("Generated: %s", format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")),
    "",
    "## Purpose",
    "Diagnostic test of whether mean baseline amplitude differs across",
    "emotion x offer_type cells. PURE DIAGNOSTIC: does NOT gate or modify",
    "the main analysis. The Alday baseline-as-covariate framework allows",
    "baseline-condition interactions and tests them in the main model.",
    "",
    "## Test",
    "Model: Baseline_c ~ emotion * offer_type + (1 | participant_id)",
    "",
    if (!is.na(interaction_p)) {
      sprintf("Omnibus emotion:offer_type interaction: p = %s",
              if (interaction_p < .001) "< .001"
              else sprintf("%.3f", interaction_p))
    } else "Omnibus interaction: not extractable",
    "",
    "## Type III ANOVA",
    if (!is.null(apa_tab)) {
      knitr::kable(apa_tab, format = "markdown", row.names = FALSE)
    } else "Test failed.",
    "",
    "## Cell means (microvolts)",
    knitr::kable(cell_means, format = "markdown", digits = 3, row.names = FALSE),
    "",
    "## Interpretation",
    "If interaction p > 0.05: baseline is balanced across conditions; no",
    "concern. If p < 0.05: condition-dependent baseline detected. The main",
    "analysis tests Baseline_c:emotion and Baseline_c:offer_type",
    "interactions in fit_stage1_bates Step 3 (LRT-based inclusion); a",
    "significant baseline-condition coupling will be retained automatically",
    "in the final model and reported in REPRODUCIBILITY.txt."
  ), out_path)
  
  invisible(out_path)
}
```

``` {r bates-engine}
# ==============================================================================
# 4. Stage 1 Engine: Bates (2015) Five-Step Random-Structure Selection
#    Combined with traditional baseline-subtraction fixed-effect specification.
# ==============================================================================
#
# FIXED-EFFECT SPECIFICATION (sensitivity analysis: traditional baseline)
# The dependent variable has been baseline-corrected upstream by subtracting
# the mean of -200 to 0 ms from the entire epoch. The fixed-effect model is
# therefore the simple two-way design: amplitude ~ emotion * offer_type. No
# Baseline_c covariate is included, and no baseline-by-condition interactions
# are tested. This is intentional and matches the standard ERP analysis
# workflow that Luck (2014) and most prior literature use. The Alday (2019)
# extended model is the primary analysis (companion script); this script is
# a sensitivity check on conclusions under the traditional approach.
#
# RANDOM-EFFECT STRUCTURE (Bates 2015 / Matuschek 2017 five-step pipeline)
#   Identical to the Alday companion script.
#   Step 1: Design-justified maximal model with main-effect random slopes and
#           full correlation parameters. Interaction random slopes are omitted
#           because cell-level variance components rarely identify in single-
#           trial EEG data with typical N (50 subjects x 30 trials/cell).
#   Step 2: Zero-correlation-parameter (ZCP) model as fallback starting point
#           for variance-component selection.
#   Step 3: LRT-based backward elimination via buildmer (alpha = 0.20 per
#           Matuschek et al. 2017, equivalent to AIC for nested two-model
#           comparisons; avoids the over-conservative model selection that
#           strict alpha = 0.05 would impose at this stage).
#   Step 4: Test whether adding correlation parameters improves fit, by
#           enumerating candidate correlated structures over the surviving
#           variance components and selecting via LRT/AIC.
#   Step 5: rePCA diagnostic on the final model documents the dimensionality
#           supported by the data, written to the reproducibility log.
# ==============================================================================

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helper: parse a fitted model's formula to identify which random slopes
# survived Step 3. Returns a character vector of slope variable names.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
extract_surviving_slopes <- function(model) {
  re_terms <- lme4::findbars(formula(model))
  surviving <- character(0)
  for (term in re_terms) {
    rhs <- deparse(term[[2]])
    rhs <- gsub("^\\s*0\\s*\\+\\s*", "", rhs)
    rhs <- gsub("^\\s*1\\s*\\+\\s*", "", rhs)
    rhs <- gsub("^\\s*1\\s*$",       "", rhs)
    rhs <- trimws(rhs)
    if (rhs == "" || rhs == "1") next
    parts <- trimws(strsplit(rhs, "\\+")[[1]])
    surviving <- c(surviving, parts)
  }
  unique(surviving)
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helper: rePCA dimensionality summary as a tidy data frame, one row per
# principal component with cumulative variance explained.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
extract_repca_summary <- function(model, group_name = "participant_id") {
  # Defensive: rePCA() requires a merMod object; lm or lmerTest objects without
  # the underlying lme4 slot will trigger getME() failures. Return an NA frame
  # so downstream count_effective_dims() returns NA cleanly.
  if (!inherits(model, "merMod")) {
    return(data.frame(component = NA_integer_, sd = NA_real_,
                      proportion_variance = NA_real_,
                      cumulative_variance = NA_real_))
  }
  pca_obj <- tryCatch(lme4::rePCA(model), error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(pca_obj) || !group_name %in% names(pca_obj)) {
    return(data.frame(component = NA_integer_, sd = NA_real_,
                      proportion_variance = NA_real_,
                      cumulative_variance = NA_real_))
  }
  imp <- summary(pca_obj[[group_name]])$importance
  data.frame(
    component = seq_len(ncol(imp)),
    sd = imp["Standard deviation", ],
    proportion_variance = imp["Proportion of Variance", ],
    cumulative_variance = imp["Cumulative Proportion", ]
  )
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helper: count effective dimensions (those reaching >= threshold cumulative
# variance). Indicates whether the random structure is overparameterized.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
count_effective_dims <- function(repca_df, threshold = 0.999) {
  if (all(is.na(repca_df$cumulative_variance))) return(NA_integer_)
  hit <- which(repca_df$cumulative_variance >= threshold)
  if (length(hit) == 0) nrow(repca_df) else hit[1]
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Step 4 helper: enumerate candidate correlated structures over surviving
# variance components, fit each, and select via LRT vs. ZCP (alpha = 0.20 per
# Matuschek et al. 2017). Returns the best-fitting model with REML refitted
# for inference.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
add_correlations_step4 <- function(model_zcp_reduced, fixed_str, data, alpha_lrt = 0.20) {
  # Defensive: if the reduced model is not an lme4 mixed model (e.g. degraded
  # to plain lm during Step 3), there are no random slopes to add correlations
  # to. Return as-is.
  if (!inherits(model_zcp_reduced, "merMod")) {
    progress_log("[Step 4] Reduced model is not a mixed model; skipping correlation tests.",
                 indent = 1)
    return(model_zcp_reduced)
  }
  
  surviving <- extract_surviving_slopes(model_zcp_reduced)
  
  if (length(surviving) == 0) {
    progress_log("[Step 4] Reduced model has only random intercept; no correlations to test.",
                 indent = 1)
    # SAFETY: do NOT use update(model_zcp_reduced, REML = TRUE). When
    # model_zcp_reduced was extracted from buildmer (bm_res@model), its
    # @call slot stores buildmer's internal data placeholder ('..2'),
    # not the actual data argument. update.merMod tries to re-evaluate
    # the call in the current environment, where '..2' does not exist,
    # producing "bad 'data': ..2 used in an incorrect context".
    # Explicit refit using formula(model) and the function's `data`
    # argument bypasses this issue.
    f_zcp_only <- formula(model_zcp_reduced)
    return(lme4::lmer(f_zcp_only, data = data, REML = TRUE,
                      control = custom_control))
  }
  
  # Build candidate set. ZCP-baseline always included for LRT baseline.
  candidates <- list()
  candidates[["ZCP_baseline"]] <- formula(model_zcp_reduced)
  
  # All-correlated candidate: (1 + s1 + s2 + ... | id)
  all_str <- paste(surviving, collapse = " + ")
  candidates[["All_correlated"]] <- as.formula(
    paste(fixed_str, "+ (1 +", all_str, "| participant_id)")
  )
  
  # Pairwise candidates: intercept correlated with one slope at a time.
  if (length(surviving) > 1) {
    for (i in seq_along(surviving)) {
      others <- setdiff(surviving, surviving[i])
      if (length(others) > 0) {
        others_terms <- paste(
          sprintf("(0 + %s | participant_id)", others),
          collapse = " + "
        )
        cand_str <- paste(fixed_str,
                          sprintf("+ (1 + %s | participant_id)", surviving[i]),
                          "+", others_terms)
      } else {
        cand_str <- paste(fixed_str,
                          sprintf("+ (1 + %s | participant_id)", surviving[i]))
      }
      candidates[[paste0("Int_with_", surviving[i])]] <- as.formula(cand_str)
    }
  }
  
  # Fit each candidate under ML for valid LRT comparison.
  total_cands <- length(candidates)
  progress_log(sprintf("[Step 4] Fitting %d candidate correlated structures...",
                       total_cands), indent = 1)
  fits <- list()
  cand_idx <- 0
  for (nm in names(candidates)) {
    cand_idx <- cand_idx + 1
    progress_log(sprintf("[Step 4 %d/%d] Trying '%s'...",
                         cand_idx, total_cands, nm), indent = 2)
    t_cand <- Sys.time()
    fit <- tryCatch(
      lme4::lmer(candidates[[nm]], data = data, REML = FALSE,
                 control = custom_control_final),
      error = function(e) NULL
    )
    fit_diag <- if (is.null(fit)) NULL else final_lmm_diagnostics(fit)
    if (!is.null(fit) && isTRUE(fit_diag$valid)) {
      fits[[nm]] <- fit
      progress_log(sprintf("[Step 4 %d/%d] '%s' converged (%s).",
                           cand_idx, total_cands, nm, format_elapsed(t_cand)),
                   indent = 3)
    } else if (!is.null(fit)) {
      progress_log(sprintf("[Step 4 %d/%d] '%s' invalid; excluded (%s): %s",
                           cand_idx, total_cands, nm, format_elapsed(t_cand),
                           format_final_lmm_diagnostics(fit_diag)),
                   indent = 3)
    } else {
      progress_log(sprintf("[Step 4 %d/%d] '%s' failed to converge (%s).",
                           cand_idx, total_cands, nm, format_elapsed(t_cand)),
                   indent = 3)
    }
  }
  
  if (is.null(fits[["ZCP_baseline"]])) {
    stop(
      "[Step 4] The buildmer-selected ZCP reference failed the mandatory ",
      "acceptance gate. Correlated candidates cannot be selected without the ",
      "prespecified LRT reference; stopping for explicit review."
    )
  }
  
  if (length(fits) == 1) {
    # Only ZCP_baseline survived (others singular). Keep it.
    progress_log("[Step 4] Only ZCP candidate viable; correlations not added.", indent = 1)
    # See safety note above re: update() and buildmer-derived models.
    f_zcp_only <- formula(model_zcp_reduced)
    m_zcp_only <- lme4::lmer(f_zcp_only, data = data, REML = TRUE,
                             control = custom_control_final)
    attr(m_zcp_only, "step4_selected") <- "ZCP_baseline"
    return(m_zcp_only)
  }
  
  # ZCP_baseline is the prespecified reference because all richer candidates are
  # nested within it. It has already passed the same mandatory acceptance gate.
  # NOTE: "baseline" here refers to the Step 4 reference model, NOT to the
  # pre-stimulus EEG baseline (Baseline_c). The two are unrelated.
  baseline_fit <- fits[["ZCP_baseline"]]
  lrt_table <- data.frame(model = character(), df_diff = integer(),
                          chisq = numeric(), p_value = numeric(),
                          AIC = numeric(), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  
  best_name <- "ZCP_baseline"
  best_fit  <- baseline_fit

  for (nm in setdiff(names(fits), "ZCP_baseline")) {
    cand <- fits[[nm]]
    lrt <- tryCatch(anova(baseline_fit, cand), error = function(e) NULL)
    if (is.null(lrt) || nrow(lrt) < 2) next
    
    p_val <- lrt$"Pr(>Chisq)"[2]
    if (is.na(p_val)) next
    
    lrt_table <- rbind(lrt_table, data.frame(
      model = nm,
      df_diff = lrt$Df[2],
      chisq = lrt$Chisq[2],
      p_value = p_val,
      AIC = AIC(cand),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    ))

    # Select candidate with lowest AIC among those passing alpha_lrt.
    if (p_val < alpha_lrt && AIC(cand) < AIC(best_fit)) {
      best_name <- nm
      best_fit  <- cand
    }
  }
  
  attr(best_fit, "step4_lrt_table") <- lrt_table
  attr(best_fit, "step4_selected") <- best_name
  
  progress_log(sprintf("[Step 4] Selected: %s (alpha_LRT = %.2f).",
                       best_name, alpha_lrt), indent = 1)
  
  f_best <- formula(best_fit)
  m_reml <- lme4::lmer(f_best, data = data, REML = TRUE,
                       control = custom_control_final)
  for (an in c("step4_lrt_table", "step4_selected")) {
    a <- attr(best_fit, an)
    if (!is.null(a)) attr(m_reml, an) <- a
  }
  m_reml
}

# ==============================================================================
# Main Stage 1 engine: full Bates 5-step pipeline + Alday 2.5 fixed structure.
# Returns the fitted model with diagnostic attributes attached.
# ==============================================================================
fit_stage1_bates <- function(data, erp_name, fixed_formula = NULL) {
  
  # Traditional baseline-subtraction sensitivity analysis: the dependent
  # variable (erp_name) has been baseline-corrected upstream by subtracting
  # the mean of -200 to 0 ms from the entire epoch. The model therefore
  # has NO Baseline_c covariate. The fixed-effect search space is the
  # simple emotion x offer_type design; no baseline-by-condition
  # interactions exist to test.
  fixed_str <- sprintf("%s ~ emotion * offer_type", erp_name)
  random_design <- add_random_contrast_columns(
    data, c("emotion", "offer_type"), "participant_id"
  )
  data <- random_design$data
  
  # Forced-include set for buildmer Step 3: theoretical core terms that must
  # remain regardless of LRT outcome. The by-subject random intercept is also
  # forced to remain because it reflects the nested data structure (trials
  # within subjects); without it, single-trial EEG data are pseudo-replicated
  # and inferential statistics are invalid.
  fixed_include <- as.formula(
    "~ emotion + offer_type + emotion:offer_type + (1 | participant_id)"
  )
  
  # Review mode: keep the saved reference model's entire fixed structure.
  # Do not reselect baseline interactions while evaluating random slopes.
  if (!is.null(fixed_formula)) {
    stopifnot(inherits(fixed_formula, "formula"),
              identical(all.vars(fixed_formula[[2]]), erp_name))
    fixed_formula <- lme4::nobars(fixed_formula)
    stopifnot(attr(terms(fixed_formula), "intercept") == 1L)
    fixed_str <- paste(deparse(fixed_formula, width.cutoff = 500L), collapse = " ")
    fixed_include <- reformulate(c(attr(terms(fixed_formula), "term.labels"),
                                   "(1 | participant_id)"))
  }

  diag_log <- list(
    component = erp_name,
    n_obs = nrow(data),
    n_subjects = dplyr::n_distinct(data$participant_id),
    random_contrast_columns = random_design$random_columns,
    random_slope_blocks = unique(unname(random_design$random_blocks)),
    step1_status = NA_character_,
    step1_pca = NULL,
    step2_status = NA_character_,
    step3_status = NA_character_,
    step3_final_formula = NA_character_,
    step4_status = NA_character_,
    step5_pca = NULL
  )
  
  # ---- STEP 1: Barr-style maximal model (including within-factor interaction slopes). ----
  progress_log(sprintf("[%s] Stage 1: Bates 5-step random-structure selection",
                       erp_name))
  progress_log(sprintf("Data: N = %d trials, %d subjects.",
                       nrow(data), dplyr::n_distinct(data$participant_id)),
               indent = 1)
  
  random_max <- sprintf(
    "(1 + %s | participant_id)",
    paste(random_design$random_columns, collapse = " + ")
  )
  f_max <- as.formula(paste(fixed_str, "+", random_max))
  diag_log$step1_formula <- paste(deparse(f_max), collapse = " ")
  progress_log(diag_log$step1_formula, indent = 2)
  
  progress_log("[Step 1] Fitting design-justified maximal model with correlations...",
               indent = 1)
  t_step1 <- Sys.time()
  m_max <- tryCatch(
    R.utils::withTimeout(
      lme4::lmer(f_max, data = data, REML = FALSE, control = custom_control),
      timeout = 300,
      onTimeout = "error"
    ),
    error = function(e) {
      progress_log(sprintf("[WARN] Maximal diagnostic failed or timed out: %s",
                           conditionMessage(e)),
                   indent = 2)
      NULL
    }
  )
  progress_log(sprintf("[Step 1] elapsed: %s", format_elapsed(t_step1)),
               indent = 2)
  
  if (!is.null(m_max)) {
    is_sing <- lme4::isSingular(m_max, tol = 1e-4)
    diag_log$step1_status <- if (is_sing) "converged_singular" else "converged_clean"
    diag_log$step1_pca <- extract_repca_summary(m_max)
    progress_log(sprintf("[Step 1] Status: %s. Effective dims = %d / %d.",
                         diag_log$step1_status,
                         count_effective_dims(diag_log$step1_pca),
                         nrow(diag_log$step1_pca)),
                 indent = 2)
  } else {
    diag_log$step1_status <- "diagnostic_failed_or_timed_out"
  }
  
  # ---- STEP 2: Zero-correlation-parameter (ZCP) model. ----
  progress_log("[Step 2] Fitting zero-correlation-parameter model...", indent = 1)
  t_step2 <- Sys.time()
  
  random_zcp <- paste(
    c("(1 | participant_id)", random_design$random_terms),
    collapse = " + "
  )
  f_zcp <- as.formula(paste(fixed_str, "+", random_zcp))
  diag_log$step2_formula <- paste(deparse(f_zcp), collapse = " ")
  progress_log(diag_log$step2_formula, indent = 2)
  blocked_terms <- make_blocked_buildmer_terms(
    f_zcp, random_design$random_blocks
  )
  
  m_zcp <- tryCatch(
    lme4::lmer(f_zcp, data = data, REML = FALSE, control = custom_control),
    error = function(e) NULL
  )
  progress_log(sprintf("[Step 2] elapsed: %s", format_elapsed(t_step2)), indent = 2)
  
  if (is.null(m_zcp)) {
    progress_log("[Step 2] Contrast-coded ZCP diagnostic fit failed; continuing to buildmer ordering.",
                 indent = 2)
    diag_log$step2_status <- "failed"
  } else {
    is_sing_zcp <- lme4::isSingular(m_zcp, tol = 1e-4)
    diag_log$step2_status <- if (is_sing_zcp) "converged_singular" else "converged_clean"
    progress_log(sprintf("[Step 2] Status: %s.", diag_log$step2_status), indent = 2)
  }
  
  # ---- STEP 3: LRT-based backward elimination via buildmer. ----
  # buildmer drops both fixed-effect baseline interactions and random-effect
  # variance components if not supported by data. Theoretical core terms are
  # protected by the 'include' argument.
  #
  # Elimination criterion uses alpha = 0.20 per Matuschek, Kliegl, Vasishth,
  # Baayen, & Bates (2017, Journal of Memory and Language). Their simulations
  # showed that alpha = 0.05 over-penalizes model complexity at the elimination
  # stage, sacrificing power to detect true fixed effects. Alpha = 0.20 is
  # approximately equivalent to AIC-based selection for nested two-model
  # comparisons and provides the optimal Type I error / power tradeoff for
  # typical psychological / psycholinguistic datasets.
  #
  # Note on buildmer API: 'crit' governs term ordering (default LRT), while
  # 'elim' governs elimination decisions. LRTalpha() generates an elimination
  # function and must be passed to 'elim', not 'crit'.
  progress_log("[Step 3] LRT-based backward elimination (buildmer, alpha = 0.20)...",
               indent = 1)
  progress_log(paste("This step iteratively tests model terms via LRT and may fit",
                     "many candidate models. With large N (>20,000 trials) and",
                     "complex random structures, expect several minutes per",
                     "component. buildmer's internal progress is shown below."),
               indent = 2)
  progress_log("[Step 3] Engineering protections active: lmerTest detached during",
               indent = 2)
  progress_log("buildmer call; withTimeout=1800s; stop on selection failure.",
               indent = 2)
  t_step3 <- Sys.time()
  
  bm_ctrl <- buildmer::buildmerControl(
    dep = erp_name,
    include = fixed_include,
    direction = c("order", "backward"),
    crit = "LRT",
    elim = buildmer::LRTalpha(0.20),
    quiet = FALSE,
    args = list(control = custom_control)
    # Note: REML is managed by buildmer internally based on whether the
    # comparison is between fixed-effect or random-effect changes. Passing
    # REML here causes a duplicate-argument error.
  )
  
  bm_res <- run_buildmer_protected(
    buildmer::buildmer,
    formula = blocked_terms, data = data,
    buildmerControl = bm_ctrl,
    timeout_sec = 1800
  )
  
  if (inherits(bm_res, "buildmer_failure")) {
    terminal_error <- identical(bm_res$type, "error") &&
      grepl("No terms left for reduction, giving up", bm_res$message, fixed = TRUE)

    if (!terminal_error) {
      stop("Step 3 buildmer selection failed or timed out: ", bm_res$message,
           ". No unvalidated ZCP fallback will be reported.")
    }

    # buildmer 2.12 can throw this terminal error after every removable random
    # slope has failed its convergence/singularity checks. The analysis already
    # defines a by-participant random intercept as the minimum viable LMM, so fit
    # that pre-specified endpoint and subject it to the unchanged downstream
    # exact-refit and final acceptance gate.
    progress_log(paste(
      "[Step 3] buildmer exhausted all removable random slopes;",
      "fitting the pre-specified random-intercept terminal model."
    ), indent = 2)
    f_terminal <- as.formula(paste(fixed_str, "+ (1 | participant_id)"))
    m_reduced <- tryCatch(
      lme4::lmer(f_terminal, data = data, REML = FALSE,
                 control = custom_control),
      error = function(e) {
        stop("Random-intercept terminal model failed: ", conditionMessage(e))
      }
    )
    diag_log$step3_status <- "buildmer_terminal_random_intercept"
  } else {
    m_reduced <- tryCatch({
      bm_res@model
    }, error = function(e) {
      stop("Could not extract the buildmer-selected model: ",
        conditionMessage(e))
    })
    diag_log$step3_status <- "buildmer_selected"
  }
  
  progress_log(sprintf("[Step 3] elapsed: %s", format_elapsed(t_step3)), indent = 2)
  
  # Sanity check: buildmer can occasionally eliminate ALL random-effect terms,
  # returning a plain `lm` object. Single-trial EEG analysis without random
  # intercepts is invalid (pseudo-replication of trials within subjects), so we
  # rebuild the minimum viable LMM with a random intercept. This branch should
  # be rare given that (1 | participant_id) is in the include set above.
  if (!inherits(m_reduced, "merMod")) {
    progress_log("[WARN] Reduced model lost all random effects; refitting with (1 | participant_id).",
                 indent = 2)
    reduced_fixed_str_recovered <- paste(deparse(formula(m_reduced)), collapse = " ")
    f_recover <- as.formula(paste(reduced_fixed_str_recovered, "+ (1 | participant_id)"))
    m_reduced <- lme4::lmer(f_recover, data = data, REML = FALSE,
                            control = custom_control)
  }
  
  diag_log$step3_final_formula <- paste(deparse(formula(m_reduced)), collapse = " ")
  progress_log(sprintf("[Step 3] Reduced formula: %s",
                       stringr::str_squish(diag_log$step3_final_formula)),
               indent = 2)
  
  # ---- STEP 4: Test correlation parameters on surviving slopes. ----
  progress_log("[Step 4] Testing correlation parameters on surviving slopes...",
               indent = 1)
  t_step4 <- Sys.time()
  
  # Reconstruct fixed-only formula from the reduced model for Step 4 candidates.
  reduced_fixed <- nobars(formula(m_reduced))
  reduced_fixed_str <- paste(deparse(reduced_fixed), collapse = " ")
  
  m_final <- add_correlations_step4(m_reduced, reduced_fixed_str, data, alpha_lrt = 0.20)
  diag_log$step4_status <- attr(m_final, "step4_selected") %||% "ZCP_kept"
  progress_log(sprintf("[Step 4] elapsed: %s. Selected: %s.",
                       format_elapsed(t_step4), diag_log$step4_status),
               indent = 2)
  
  # ---- STEP 5: rePCA diagnostic on final model. ----
  diag_log$step5_pca <- extract_repca_summary(m_final)
  step5_eff <- count_effective_dims(diag_log$step5_pca)
  step5_nom <- nrow(diag_log$step5_pca)
  progress_log(sprintf("[Step 5] Final model dimensionality: %s effective / %s nominal.",
                       if (is.na(step5_eff)) "NA" else as.character(step5_eff),
                       if (is.na(step5_nom)) "NA" else as.character(step5_nom)),
               indent = 1)
  
  # ---- Defensive REML guard. ----
  # 
  # Several paths through add_correlations_step4 and fit_stage1_bates can
  # return an LMM in ML state (REML=FALSE). lmerTest::anova(ddf="Satterthwaite")
  # expects REML by default. Refit REML here unconditionally so the downstream
  # ANOVA cascade has a clean input.
  # 
  # SAFETY: do NOT use update() because m_final may be a buildmer @model
  # object whose @call references buildmer's internal '..2' placeholder,
  # which fails outside buildmer's scope. Refit explicitly from formula
  # and the local `data` argument.
  if (inherits(m_final, "merMod")) {
    is_reml <- tryCatch(lme4::isREML(m_final), error = function(e) FALSE)
    if (!isTRUE(is_reml)) {
      progress_log("[Final] Refitting LMM with REML=TRUE for Satterthwaite compatibility.",
                   indent = 1)
      f_final <- formula(m_final)
      m_final_reml <- tryCatch(
        lme4::lmer(f_final, data = data, REML = TRUE, control = custom_control),
        error = function(e) {
          progress_log(sprintf("[Final] REML refit failed: %s; retaining ML fit.",
                               conditionMessage(e)), indent = 2)
          NULL
        }
      )
      if (!is.null(m_final_reml)) {
        existing_attrs <- attributes(m_final)[c("step4_selected",
                                                "step4_lrt_table")]
        for (an in names(existing_attrs)) {
          if (!is.null(existing_attrs[[an]])) {
            attr(m_final_reml, an) <- existing_attrs[[an]]
          }
        }
        m_final <- m_final_reml
      }
    }
  }
  
  # ---- Mandatory final-model validation. ----
  # Keep derivative-free fits during selection, then refit the exact selected
  # formula with derivatives before any inference, output, or serialization.
  progress_log("[Final] Refitting exact LMM formula with derivatives enabled.",
               indent = 1)
  m_final <- refit_and_validate_final_lmm(m_final, data)
  diag_log$final_validation <- attr(m_final, "final_validation")
  diag_log$final_random_tier <- attr(m_final, "final_random_tier")
  diag_log$step5_pca <- extract_repca_summary(m_final)
  progress_log(sprintf("[Final] Acceptance gate: %s",
                       format_final_lmm_diagnostics(diag_log$final_validation)),
               indent = 1)

  # ---- Defensive lmerTest class upgrade. ----
  # 
  # CRITICAL for Satterthwaite/KR p-values. When fit via lme4::lmer() (rather
  # than lmerTest::lmer()), the resulting object has class "lmerMod" only.
  # Calling anova(model, ddf="Satterthwaite") on a bare lmerMod does NOT
  # dispatch to lmerTest's S4 method; lme4's base anova() handles it,
  # silently ignoring the ddf argument and returning a table with F values
  # but NO Pr(>F) and NO NumDF/DenDF columns. The downstream cascade then
  # detects "no Pr column" and falls through to Wald.
  # 
  # The fix is to upgrade the class via lmerTest::as_lmerModLmerTest() (a
  # free no-refit operation that registers the model with lmerTest's
  # df-computation machinery). buildmer internally fits via lmerTest::lmer()
  # so its @model output may already be lmerModLmerTest; but our 
  # add_correlations_step4 refits via lme4::lmer() in many paths, losing the
  # lmerTest class. This guard ensures the final returned model is dispatch-
  # ready regardless of which fallback path was taken.
  if (inherits(m_final, "merMod") && !inherits(m_final, "lmerModLmerTest")) {
    m_final_lt <- tryCatch(
      lmerTest::as_lmerModLmerTest(m_final),
      error = function(e) {
        progress_log(sprintf("[Final] lmerTest class upgrade failed: %s",
                             conditionMessage(e)), indent = 2)
        NULL
      }
    )
    if (!is.null(m_final_lt)) {
      existing_attrs <- attributes(m_final)[c(
        "step4_selected", "step4_lrt_table", "final_validation",
        "final_random_tier"
      )]
      for (an in names(existing_attrs)) {
        if (!is.null(existing_attrs[[an]])) {
          attr(m_final_lt, an) <- existing_attrs[[an]]
        }
      }
      m_final <- m_final_lt
      progress_log("[Final] LMM upgraded to lmerModLmerTest for Satt/KR dispatch.",
                   indent = 1)
    }
  }
  
  attr(m_final, "bates_diag") <- diag_log
  m_final
}
```
